mainTopic: Eating קדשים while the משכן travels, the stone or copper מזבח of שילה and the heavenly fire, and why the מזבח was enlarged in the second בית המקדש
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: sacrificial food may still be eaten after the לויים take apart the משכן, as long as the מזבח has not been moved. The פסוק 'ונסע אהל מועד' shows that the אהל מועד keeps its status even while traveling, so the food is not פסול as יוצא. Next, רב הונא says in the name of רב that the מזבח in שילה was made of stones, and a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב supports him. רב אחא בר אמי objects from a ברייתא that says the heavenly fire stayed on the copper מזבח until שלמה. The גמרא gives two answers. One follows רבי נתן: the מזבח of שילה was copper, filled with stones. The other says the fire never fully left, and it either sent sparks or moved like a guest between the two מזבחות. Then the גמרא asks why the returning exiles made the מזבח bigger. רב יוסף says they needed more room because the second בית המקדש had no fire from heaven. בר קפרא says they extended it over the שיתין, because the poured liquids must go on top of the מזבח, and he explains 'מזבח אדמה' as a מזבח attached to the ground.

steps.title: Food is still allowed after the Tabernacle is taken down
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that sacrificial food may still be eaten after the לויים take apart the משכן, as long as the altar is still in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And after the Levites take apart the Tabernacle.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא. It says that קדשים may still be eaten after the לויים have taken the משכן apart, as long as the altar has not been moved yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a moment in between. The walls are down, but the מזבח is still standing. The ברייתא rules that eating is still allowed at this point.

keyTerms.meaning: The Levites, who took the משכן apart and carried it
The Tabernacle, the portable sanctuary in the desert
Taking apart, dismantling

phrases.english: And after the Levites take apart
the Tabernacle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that was quoted before this section begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after the משכן is taken apart, קדשים may be eaten as long as the altar is still in place.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא needed to say this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the new point of the ברייתא. Without it, we might think the food became פסול as 'יוצא' once the walls came down.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the food became disqualified as having gone out. So it teaches us that it did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא had to teach this rule. It shows the mistake we might otherwise have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the walls of the courtyard are gone, you could think the food is now 'outside' its holy area. That would make it פסול as יוצא. The ברייתא teaches that this is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken idea we could have had)
Sacrificial food that left its permitted area and became פסול
It teaches us (the new point)

phrases.english: You might have said:
they became disqualified as having gone out;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the sacrificial foods. With the walls down, it is as if the food is now outside.

phrases.english: it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the new point of the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking down the walls does not make the food פסול as יוצא.

steps.title: Challenge: maybe the food really is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should not accept the 'mistaken' idea. Perhaps without walls the food really is יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. It asks why the idea from step 2 should be wrong, since the walls really are gone. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that the food is פסול seems to make sense. Without the walls, there is no clear holy area left. So the גמרא wants a source that shows the place keeps its status.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so (a challenge to the stated rule)

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: In other words: maybe the food really did become disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling explained in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the food is not פסול as יוצא once the walls come down.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without walls there seems to be no holy area, so the food should count as having gone out.

steps.title: The verse shows the Tent keeps its status while traveling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'ונסע אהל מועד'. Even while traveling, it is still the אהל מועד, so the food is not יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the Tent of Meeting shall travel.' Even though it traveled, it is still the Tent of Meeting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. The תורה still calls it 'אהל מועד' while it is traveling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ונסע אהל מועד' teach that the משכן keeps its holy status even while it is being moved. So the food is not considered outside its area, even with the walls down.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, another name for the משכן
And it shall travel

steps.whatToRemember: While it is being moved, the משכן is still called 'אהל מועד'. So sacrificial food is not פסול as יוצא just because the walls are down.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'And the Tent of Meeting shall travel' –
even though it traveled,
it is still the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without walls, the food would count as having left its holy area.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משכן keeps its status as אהל מועד even while traveling, so the food is not פסול.

steps.title: The altar in Shiloh was made of stone
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: רב הונא in the name of רב says the מזבח in שילה was made of stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: The altar of Shiloh was made of stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about the altar. רב says that the altar in שילה was built of stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement about what the altar was made of in a later period, the time of שילה. Proof for it comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Altar
Shiloh, where the משכן stood after the people entered the land
Stones

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the altar of the desert משכן, which was covered with copper. רב is talking about the altar in שילה, a later period.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The altar of Shiloh –
was made of stones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The altar in שילה was made of stones.

steps.title: Three times 'stones' means three stone altars
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the word 'אבנים' three times as pointing to three stone altars: שילה, נוב and גבעון, and the בית עולמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, why does the verse say 'stones,' 'stones,' 'stones,' three times? One is for Shiloh, one for Nov and Gibeon, and one for the Eternal House.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב's statement. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב explains why the תורה says 'אבנים' three times about the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each mention of 'stones' points to a different stone altar. One of them is the altar of שילה, which matches what רב said. The others are the altar of נוב and גבעון, counted together, and the altar of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say (asking what extra words teach)
Nov and Gibeon, places where the altar stood after שילה
The Eternal House: the בית המקדש in ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the altar of שילה was stone. This is based on the three mentions of 'אבנים': שילה, נוב and גבעון, and the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Why does the verse say
'stones,' 'stones,' 'stones,' three times?
One is for Shiloh,
and one is for Nov and Gibeon,
and one is for the Eternal House.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב's statement in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that the altar of שילה was made of stones.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reading the three mentions of 'אבנים' as three stone altars.

steps.title: The fire stayed on the copper altar until Shlomo
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אמי quotes a ברייתא: the heavenly fire from the time of משה stayed on the copper מזבח until שלמה. If שילה had a stone מזבח, the fire would have left the copper one much earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אמי objects: the fire that came down from heaven in the days of משה only left the copper מזבח in the days of שלמה. The fire that came down in the days of שלמה stayed until מנשה came and removed it. But if רב הונא is right that the מזבח in שילה was stone, the fire would have left the copper מזבח already back then!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's statement from step 5, that the מזבח in שילה was made of stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the fire stayed on the copper מזבח until שלמה. If שילה already used a stone מזבח, the copper one was no longer in use, so the fire should have left it in the time of שילה. That clashes with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: the copper altar that משה made in the מדבר
went away, departed
and if it is so, meaning if your claim were true
from earlier, at the start

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ami raises an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אֵשׁ שֶׁיָּרְדָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה –
phrases.english: The fire that came down from heaven in the days of Moshe
did not leave the copper altar
until the days of Shlomo,
and the fire that came down in the days of Shlomo

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִסְתַּלְּקָה עַד שֶׁבָּא מְנַשֶּׁה וְסִילְּקָהּ.
phrases.english: did not leave until Menashe came and removed it.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רב הונא is right that the מזבח in שילה was made of stones.

phrases.english: then it would have left much earlier!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's claim, which step 6 had just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that the מזבח in שילה was stone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A stone מזבח in שילה would mean the copper מזבח stopped being used before שלמה. Yet the ברייתא says the fire stayed on the copper מזבח until שלמה.

steps.title: רב הונא follows Rabbi Natan: a copper altar filled with stones
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds like רבי נתן, who says the מזבח of שילה was copper, hollow, and filled with stones. So the copper מזבח was still in use and the fire stayed on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said his view following רבי נתן. A ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says the מזבח of שילה was made of copper, hollow, and filled with stones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רב הונא's 'stones' as the stones that filled the inside of a copper מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outside of the מזבח in שילה was copper, so it was still the copper מזבח and the fire could stay on it until שלמה. It was 'of stones' only because stones filled its hollow inside.

keyTerms.meaning: hollow
and filled with stones

phrases.english: He said it following Rabbi Natan,
as it was taught: Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: מִזְבֵּחַ שֶׁל שִׁילֹה – שֶׁל נְחוֹשֶׁת הָיָה,
phrases.english: the altar of Shiloh was made of copper,
hollow and filled with stones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the claim: the 'stone' altar was really a copper altar filled with stones.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא meant the מזבח in שילה was fully stone and replaced the copper one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזבח in שילה was copper on the outside with stones inside, so the fire stayed on the copper מזבח until שלמה.

steps.title: The fire never left in a way that it was gone for good
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another answer. 'Did not leave' means the fire did not leave and become completely gone. The stone מזבח could have existed in שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: what does 'it did not leave' mean? It did not leave in a way that it was completely gone.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the challenge. This one keeps רב הונא's stone מזבח and reads the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mean the fire stayed only on the copper מזבח. It means the fire never fully stopped being present until שלמה, even after a stone מזבח was also in use in שילה.

keyTerms.meaning: to become nothing, completely gone
what, what does it mean

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What does 'it did not leave' mean?
It did not leave in a way that it was completely gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מַאי לֹא נִסְתַּלְּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Did not leave' means the fire stayed only on the copper מזבח, so there was no stone מזבח before שלמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Did not leave' means the fire was never completely gone, which fits a stone מזבח in שילה.

steps.title: What does 'not completely gone' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly it means that the fire did not leave to become completely gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step. It asks how the fire was still present if sacrifices were brought on the stone מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer is unclear. If the main מזבח was stone, in what way was the fire from משה still there? The next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? asking for an explanation

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a clearer explanation of step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the fire stayed present without being fully gone

steps.title: Sparks or a visiting guest
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say the fire sent out sparks to the stone מזבח. רב פפא says the fire was like a guest, sometimes on one מזבח and sometimes on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן say: it would send out a spark. רב פפא says: it acted like a guest, sometimes here and sometimes there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two explanations of how the fire was still present in שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבנן, the fire stayed on the copper מזבח but shot sparks over to the stone one. According to רב פפא, the fire itself moved back and forth between the two מזבחות. Either way, it never fully left until שלמה.

keyTerms.meaning: a spark
sends out
a guest, a visitor
sometimes

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the challenge on רב הונא: (1) the מזבח of שילה was copper filled with stones, like רבי נתן; (2) the fire was never completely gone, either sending sparks or moving like a guest between the two מזבחות.

phrases.english: The Rabbis say:
It would send out a spark.
phrases.notes: The spark went from the copper מזבח to the stone מזבח.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
It acted like a guest,
sometimes here and sometimes there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire either sent sparks to the stone מזבח (רבנן) or moved between the two מזבחות like a guest (רב פפא).

steps.title: The returning exiles made the altar bigger
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: a משנה says that when the people came back from גלות, they added four אמות on the south and four on the west of the מזבח, in a corner shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: when the people of the exile came up, they added four אמות to the מזבח on the south and four אמות on the west, shaped like a gamma.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about the size of the מזבח in the second בית המקדש. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The additions were only on two sides, south and west, so together they formed a corner shape. This made the מזבח larger than the one from the first בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: the people who returned from exile in בבל
cubits, a unit of length
shaped like the Greek letter gamma, a corner shape

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מדות.

phrases.english: And when the people of the exile came up,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹסִיפוּ עָלָיו אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת מִן הַדָּרוֹם
phrases.english: they added to it four cubits on the south
and four cubits on the west,
like the shape of a gamma.
phrases.notes: Gamma is a Greek letter shaped like a corner (Γ). The two additions met at one corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the size of the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second בית המקדש, four אמות were added to the מזבח on the south and four on the west.

steps.title: Why did they make it bigger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the returning exiles enlarged the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step. It asks for the reason behind the enlargement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first בית המקדש's מזבח was already set at a fixed size, so changing it needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מזבח was enlarged in the second בית המקדש

steps.title: The old size was not enough
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the old מזבח was not big enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: because it was not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the reason: the original size of the מזבח was too small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enlargement was done out of practical need, because the old size was not large enough for what was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: was enough, was sufficient

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because it was not enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא סָפַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first בית המקדש's מזבח was not large enough.

steps.title: אביי challenges: fewer people, yet the מזבח was too small?
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer. The first בית המקדש served a huge nation and the old מזבח was enough, so how could it be too small for the much smaller nation of the second בית המקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Now think about it. In the first Temple, where the verse says 'Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea,' the altar was big enough. In the second Temple, where the verse says the whole congregation was only about forty thousand, it was not big enough?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's claim from step 14 that the old מזבח was not big enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי compares the two populations using two פסוקים. In the first בית המקדש the people were 'like the sand of the sea,' and in the second they were only about forty thousand. More people means more קרבנות, so if the smaller מזבח worked for the bigger crowd, it should surely work for the smaller one.

keyTerms.meaning: The first בית המקדש, built by שלמה
The second בית המקדש, built after the return from גלות בבל
Here it means 'was enough' or 'was big enough.' It does not mean 'doubt' in this place
Ten thousand

steps.confusionAlert: The word סְפֵק / סָפֵק here does NOT mean 'doubt.' It comes from the word for 'enough' (like מספיק).

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב יוסף, who just said the old מזבח was not big enough.

phrases.english: as the sand that is by the sea" — it was enough for them;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַשְׁתָּא מִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the old מזבח was not big enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bigger population brings more קרבנות. If the old מזבח was enough for a huge nation, it must have been enough for a much smaller one.

steps.title: רב יוסף answers: the first Temple had fire from heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that in the first בית המקדש a fire from heaven helped burn the קרבנות quickly. In the second there was no heavenly fire, so they needed more space.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, in the first Temple, a fire from heaven helped them. Here, in the second Temple, no fire from heaven helped them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his answer by pointing to a difference between the two Temples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size of the crowd is not the only thing that matters. In the first בית המקדש, אש של שמים burned the offerings fast, so a smaller מזבח was enough. Without that help in the second בית המקדש, the קרבנות took longer to burn and needed more room.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire from heaven that came down on the מזבח
Helped them
There / here. Here they mean the first בית המקדש and the second

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, a fire from heaven helped them,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא אֵין אֵשׁ שֶׁל שָׁמַיִם מְסַיַּיעְתָּן.
phrases.english: here, no fire from heaven helped them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The size of the population decides how big the מזבח must be
steps.terutzMaskana: The heavenly fire in the first בית המקדש made a smaller מזבח enough. The second בית המקדש lacked that fire and needed a larger one.

steps.title: Ravin's report: they enlarged it to cover the שיתין
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a different reason in the name of בר קפרא. The מזבח was made bigger so that it would extend over the שיתין, the pits under the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said that רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of בר קפרא: They added on to cover the שיתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question of step 13: why did the exiles make the מזבח bigger?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the reason was space for burning. בר קפרא says the reason was about the שיתין, the pits where the poured wine and water drained. The מזבח was stretched so that it sat over those pits.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and reported a teaching
Pits under the מזבח where the poured liquids (נסכים) drained down
They added on, made bigger

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
They added on over the shitin.
phrases.notes: The שיתין are the pits under the מזבח where the poured wine and water flowed down.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 13, instead of רב יוסף's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the returning exiles made the מזבח bigger
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They extended it to reach over the שיתין

steps.title: Why they changed: from solid earth to 'drinking is like eating'
steps.stepSummary: At first they thought 'מזבח אדמה' meant the מזבח had to be completely solid earth. Later they held that the poured liquids, like the burned offerings, must go on top of the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they held that 'an altar of earth' means it must be solid, filled with earth. But in the end they held that the altar's drinking is like its eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind בר קפרא's answer: why the מזבח now had to cover the שיתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first view, the מזבח had to be solid earth, so no holes could run through it into the שיתין. The new view says the נסכים (the altar's 'drink') must be poured on top of the מזבח, just like the offerings (its 'food') are burned on top. So they extended the מזבח over the שיתין and made holes so the liquids could drain down through it.

keyTerms.meaning: At first they held
'An altar of earth,' from the פסוק in שמות
Solid, filled in, with no holes
The altar's 'drinking' (poured liquids) is like its 'eating' (burned offerings): both must be on top of it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a new understanding of a פסוק led to a real change in how the מזבח was built.

phrases.english: At first they held:
"An altar of earth"
— means that it is solid, filled with earth.
But in the end they held:
drinking is like eating,
phrases.notes: The poured liquids are the altar's 'drink.' Like its 'food,' the offerings, they must be put right on top of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind בר קפרא's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first view required a solid earth מזבח. The later view held שתיה כאכילה, so the מזבח was extended over the שיתין.

steps.title: So what does 'altar of earth' mean now?
steps.stepSummary: If the מזבח no longer has to be solid earth, the גמרא asks how we should now understand the words 'מזבח אדמה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what, then, is the meaning of 'an altar of earth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move: it asks for a new meaning of the פסוק, since the old meaning was dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later view gave up the idea that 'מזבח אדמה' means solid earth. But the words of the פסוק must still teach something, so the גמרא asks what they teach.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "an altar of earth"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the פסוק means under the later view of step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new meaning of 'מזבח אדמה' now that solid earth is not required

steps.title: New meaning: the מזבח must be attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: 'מזבח אדמה' now means the מזבח must be attached to the ground. It may not be built on top of arches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that the altar is attached to the earth, so that one may not build it on top of arches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 19 by giving the פסוק a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'made of solid earth,' the words now mean 'connected to the earth.' This still allows holes into the שיתין, but it forbids building the מזבח raised up on arches with empty space beneath it.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached to the ground
Arches or vaults

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why the exiles made the מזבח bigger. רב יוסף says they needed more room because there was no heavenly fire. בר קפרא says it was to reach over the שיתין, because the poured liquids must go on top of the מזבח. Under his view, 'מזבח אדמה' means attached to the ground.

phrases.english: — that it is attached to the earth;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִבְנֶנּוּ לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי כִּיפִּים
phrases.english: that one should not build it on top of arches
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next דף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מזבח אדמה' means the מזבח must be attached to the ground and not built on arches
